overview: Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHCs) is a sub-scheme under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) launched by the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs to provide dignified affordable rental housing to urban migrants and poor from EWS/LIG categories near their workplaces. The scheme operates through two models: Model-1 involves converting existing government-funded vacant houses into ARHCs via Public-Private Partnership or public agencies, while Model-2 involves construction, operation, and maintenance of ARHCs by public/private entities on their own vacant land. Projects are to be operated for a minimum period of 25 years and aim to unlock vacant housing stock, promote investment in rental housing, and improve living conditions for urban migrants/poor.
objectives: Provide ease of living to urban migrants/poor by ensuring access to dignified affordable rental housing close to their workplace
Unlock existing vacant housing stock and make it available in urban space
Propel new investment opportunities and promote entrepreneurship in the rental housing sector
Create a conducive ecosystem for public/private entities to leverage investment in rental housing
Prevent growth of slums by providing affordable rental accommodation
Improve productivity of urban migrants/poor by reducing commute time and improving living conditions
Support the vision of 'AatmaNirbhar Bharat' and the larger goal of 'Housing for All' under PMAY-U
eligibility: Beneficiaries for ARHCs are urban migrants/poor from EWS/LIG categories. Under Model-1, concessionaires are selected through transparent bidding process by States/UTs/ULBs for repairing, retrofitting, developing, operating, and transferring ARHCs. Under Model-2, public/private entities with their own vacant land can apply via Expression of Interest (EoI) to construct, operate, and maintain ARHCs. Entities must comply with NBC/State/Local Authority norms for dwelling units and dormitories, and projects must include at least 40 dwelling units or equivalent dormitory beds.
benefits: Incentives/benefits include: exemption of income tax and GST on profits from ARHC operations; concessional project finance at lower interest rates through Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) and Priority Sector Lending (PSL); 50% additional FAR/FSI free of cost; single window approval system for design/drawings and statutory approvals within 30 days; provision of trunk infrastructure (road, water, sanitation, electricity) at no additional cost; municipal services levied at par with residential projects; use permission changes if needed; and Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) for adopting innovative technologies.
financial_support: Financial support includes concessional loans from Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) under Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) and Priority Sector Lending (PSL) by commercial banks at lower interest rates. Viability Gap Funding (VGF) may be provided from central assistance released to States/UTs for JnNURM/RAY projects if needed. Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) of Rs. 1,00,000 per double bedroom unit, Rs. 60,000 per single bedroom unit, and Rs. 20,000 per dormitory bed is available for projects using identified innovative technologies. Under Model-1, concessionaires invest their own funds to make houses livable; under Model-2, entities bear the investment for construction on their vacant land.
application_process: 1. For Model-1: States/UTs/ULBs prepare inventory of government-funded vacant houses, customize and issue RFP based on model RFP from MoHUA, conduct pre-bid meeting, receive and evaluate technical and financial bids, select concessionaire, sign concession agreement. 2. For Model-2: MoHUA issues Expression of Interest (EoI); entities submit application with documents on ARHC website; concerned ULBs shortlist entities based on eligibility; shortlisted entities submit Detailed Project Report (DPR) to ULB for approval; upon approval, entities construct, operate, and maintain ARHCs on their vacant land for 25 years.
required_documents: Details of eligible similar nature of works completed in last seven years
Performance Report of Works referred in Form-C
Site laboratory and testing of materials setup
Suggestive list of plant and equipment at site
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round through EoI for Model-2 and RFP notices for Model-1 as issued by States/UTs/ULBs.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
caveats: Projects under ARHCs will be applicable for consideration and funding till PMAY (U) Mission period i.e. March 2022, though approved projects will be funded for another 18 months to enable completion
ARHCs must be exclusively used for rental housing for a minimum period of 25 years
A maximum of 33% dwelling units in double bedroom form is permissible in any ARHC project
Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) is released only for projects using identified innovative technologies
Beneficiaries are restricted to urban migrants/poor from EWS/LIG categories
